item.title: US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed launches 'Habibi PAC' days after historic election win
item.description: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported.
item.content:encoded:
US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed launches 'Habibi PAC' days after historic election win Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported. ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 21:32 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 21:32 IST

Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported. According to Al Jazeera, citing a filing submitted to the Federal Election Commission (FEC) on Thursday, Habibi PAC has been registered as a leadership PAC sponsored by El-Sayed. Such committees operate separately from a politician's own election campaign and are used to raise and spend funds in support of other political candidates and political activities. The name 'Habibi', an Arabic term of endearment meaning 'my dear' or 'my beloved', is a phrase El-Sayed frequently used during his election campaign. He also used the expression while addressing US Vice President JD Vance during his victory speech in Detroit, saying, "JD, habibi, there is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January." El-Sayed is among several newly elected Democratic lawmakers who have registered leadership PACs following Tuesday's election, according to FEC filings. Others include Arizona Congressman-elect Amish Shah, who registered 'PACStreet Boy', Iowa Senator-elect Josh Turek, who launched 'WheelPAC', and North Carolina Senator-elect Roy Cooper, who registered 'One NC PAC', as reported by Al Jazeera. According to Al Jazeera, citing OpenSecrets, leadership PACs are often used by ambitious lawmakers to build influence among their colleagues and strengthen their prospects of securing party leadership positions or committee chairmanships. They typically contribute to other lawmakers, political parties and political committees. During the 2024 election cycle, leadership PACs contributed USD 79.3 million to federal candidates. While most of the contributions went to Republican candidates, a Democratic leadership PAC emerged as the largest individual donor, Al Jazeera reported, citing OpenSecrets. El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, defeated Republican candidate Mike Rogers following a campaign in which US President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Senator Ted Cruz questioned his loyalty, called him a "jihadist" and attempted to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood movement without providing evidence. Getting money out of politics was among El-Sayed's central campaign pledges. During his victory speech, he highlighted the significance of his electoral success, saying that in a contest between money and the people, "the many can win". His victory came amid the most expensive midterm election on record. According to Al Jazeera, an analysis of FEC data by OpenSecrets noted that total spending in the election cycle is expected to reach USD 11.9 billion, compared with USD 8.9 billion in 2022. Outside spending, largely driven by super PACs, is projected to reach USD 3.9 billion, marking an 85 per cent increase from the 2022 midterm elections. Meanwhile, so-called dark money contributions from donors whose identities are not disclosed have already reached at least USD 1.47 billion, surpassing the previous record of USD 1.35 billion set during the 2024 election cycle, which also included the presidential race. According to Al Jazeera, OpenSecrets found that conservative groups outspent liberal groups by approximately USD 360 million in outside spending, while Democratic candidates were expected to outspend their Republican counterparts by around USD 800 million. Political action committees, or PACs, are organisations that raise and spend money to support or oppose candidates for public office. Leadership PACs, in particular, allow elected officials and lawmakers to support other candidates and political organisations independently of their own campaign committees. (ANI)

item.title: Gaza rains flood 70,000 tents housing displaced Palestinians as first winter storm hits Strip
item.description: Around 70,000 tents sheltering displaced Palestinian families have been flooded across the Gaza Strip within 12 hours of the first winter storm of the season, leaving thousands exposed to heavy ...
item.content:encoded:
Gaza rains flood 70,000 tents housing displaced Palestinians as first winter storm hits Strip Around 70,000 tents sheltering displaced Palestinian families have been flooded across the Gaza Strip within 12 hours of the first winter storm of the season, leaving thousands exposed to heavy rainfall, rising water levels and harsh weather conditions, Al Jazeera reported, citing Gaza's Government Media Office. ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 21:17 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 21:17 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Palestine

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Around 70,000 tents sheltering displaced Palestinian families have been flooded across the Gaza Strip within 12 hours of the first winter storm of the season, leaving thousands exposed to heavy rainfall, rising water levels and harsh weather conditions, Al Jazeera reported, citing Gaza's Government Media Office. In a statement issued on Saturday, the Government Media Office estimated the initial losses from the flooding at approximately USD 3 million. It also reported that dozens of walls had collapsed, several people had sustained injuries and damaged buildings at risk of further collapse posed an additional threat to residents. The office held Israel "fully responsible" for a disaster resulting from the continued closure of border crossings and restrictions on the entry of shelter and reconstruction materials. It also called on the international community and United Nations agencies to intervene immediately to protect displaced Palestinians, Al Jazeera reported. According to Gaza's Civil Defence agency, rescue teams received around 1,500 distress calls within just 10 hours after rainfall began early Saturday. Water levels at several displacement sites reportedly rose by 30 to 40 centimetres. Describing the situation, Civil Defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal told Al Jazeera that several shelter centres had been completely inundated, forcing residents to leave their tents. “What we feared has actually happened,” Basal told Al Jazeera. “A few shelter centres were completely flooded, and everyone inside them has now been forced out into the unknown," he added. He warned that vulnerable groups, particularly premature babies, elderly people and those suffering from illnesses, faced the greatest risks amid the worsening weather conditions. “Those living in tents are at risk of death at any moment, and of illness at any moment,” he said, as quoted by Al Jazeera. The storm also caused further damage to buildings already weakened during Israel's war on the enclave, which began in October 2023. Gaza's Civil Defence agency said rescue teams evacuated residents from a building in the central Nuseirat area after it partially collapsed amid strong winds and rainfall. In northern Gaza, the wall of another building collapsed following heavy rainfall, injuring two people, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. Footage from displacement camps in Gaza City, Khan Younis and Deir el-Balah showed families wading through ankle-deep water, with mattresses and blankets soaked in rainwater and children standing barefoot in muddy and sewage-contaminated pools. In Khan Younis, Al Jazeera reported that rainfall had begun around 10 pm (local time) on Friday in al-Mawasi, the coastal area in southern Gaza where more than 900,000 displaced people are sheltering. Gaza's emergency committee warned that more than one million displaced people were facing a difficult winter and said the territory urgently required approximately 200,000 tents, along with heating supplies. Highlighting the limited resources available to rescue teams, Raed al-Dahshan, director of Civil Defence in Gaza, told Al Jazeera that crews lacked even basic shelter materials to assist affected families. “Civil defence does not have a single tarpaulin or a single tent,” al-Dahshan said. “We deal only with saving lives, and that is not enough," he added. Aid organisations have blamed Israeli restrictions on the entry of shelter materials for the shortage of essential supplies. The rainfall has also affected Gaza's already battered healthcare infrastructure. Mohammed Abu Salmiya, director of al-Shifa Medical Complex in Gaza City, told Al Jazeera that the hospital's emergency department was flooded and remained out of service for approximately four hours. He warned that the mixing of sewage with rainwater inside displacement tents could lead to an increase in gastrointestinal, respiratory and skin infections. “We will see many deaths, in the dozens and perhaps the hundreds, among newborns who need warmth in these tents,” Abu Salmiya said. In Gaza City port, Al Jazeera reported that thousands of displaced families had established tents along the shoreline, leaving them exposed to strong winds and rising tides. Many of the tents currently sheltering displaced Palestinians were initially set up during the first year of displacement and are now in their fourth year of use. Families have repeatedly patched and re-stitched them to keep them functional. Under the humanitarian protocol of the ceasefire, the tents were supposed to be replaced with caravans, which Israel has not allowed into the territory. Highlighting the desperation among displaced families, one man living in a tent along the beach told Al Jazeera, “They pushed us west towards the sea. Why don’t they just throw us into the sea and be done with it?” Meanwhile, Mohammed Salha, director of the Palestinian NGO Network, told Al Jazeera that only 180 to 200 trucks were entering Gaza daily, significantly below the 600 trucks agreed upon under the humanitarian protocol of the ceasefire. He added that only around 40 of the trucks were carrying humanitarian assistance. He also said that approximately 50,000 tents were waiting on the Egyptian side of the border. "We must respond before the disaster happens," he said, describing international pressure on Israel to allow additional supplies into Gaza as "timid". (ANI)

item.title: Pakistan smothers with smog as pollution levels reach hazardous extremes
item.description: Severe smog and worsening air quality have engulfed several major cities across Pakistan’s Punjab province, including Islamabad and Rawalpindi, exposing residents to serious health risks.
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan smothers with smog as pollution levels reach hazardous extremes Severe smog and worsening air quality have engulfed several major cities across Pakistan’s Punjab province, including Islamabad and Rawalpindi, exposing residents to serious health risks. ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 18:58 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 18:58 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Severe smog and worsening air quality have engulfed several major cities across Pakistan’s Punjab province, including Islamabad and Rawalpindi, exposing residents to serious health risks. The worsening pollution has triggered a surge in respiratory illnesses, asthma, throat infections, eye irritation, colds and persistent coughing, as reported by The Express Tribune. According to The Express Tribune, the scale of the health emergency is becoming increasingly evident in Rawalpindi, where 2,961 patients suffering from smog-related ailments sought treatment at the outpatient departments and emergency wards of three allied hospitals within just 48 hours. Most of those affected were elderly men and women, highlighting the vulnerability of older residents to hazardous air conditions. Air quality readings have painted an alarming picture across the region. Islamabad recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 187, while Rawalpindi registered 179. Lahore's AQI surged to 530, whereas Multan recorded an exceptionally dangerous 719. Faisalabad stood at 371, while Gujranwala recorded levels between 600 and 660. Jhang's AQI reached 678, while Murree, popularly known as the Queen of Hills, crossed 123. Industrial centres such as Gujranwala, Faisalabad and Jhang are among the worst affected. Authorities fear that pollution levels could rise further if rainfall does not occur over the following three days. Medical professionals and health authorities have advised residents to wear protective masks, particularly outdoors. Children and individuals with respiratory conditions have been urged to avoid unnecessary outdoor exposure. People have also been advised to keep doors and windows shut during morning and evening hours and seek medical guidance before using eye drops, as cited by The Express Tribune. The Environmental Protection Department has identified brick kilns, stone crushers, industrial emissions, vehicle exhaust, crop-residue burning and the extraction of black oil through burning discarded tyres as major contributors to the crisis. Smoke-emitting vehicles have been described as a particularly serious pollution source, as reported by The Express Tribune. (ANI)

item.title: Balochistan parties announce province-wide shutdown amid deepening crisis
item.description: Leaders of several major political parties in Balochistan have announced a province-wide shutdown strike on November 19, followed by demonstrations at all district headquarters, accusing the ...
item.content:encoded:
Balochistan parties announce province-wide shutdown amid deepening crisis Leaders of several major political parties in Balochistan have announced a province-wide shutdown strike on November 19, followed by demonstrations at all district headquarters, accusing the government of failing to address the province’s worsening political, security and economic crises, as reported by The Express Tribune. ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 17:38 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 17:38 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Leaders of several major political parties in Balochistan have announced a province-wide shutdown strike on November 19, followed by demonstrations at all district headquarters, accusing the government of failing to address the province’s worsening political, security and economic crises, as reported by The Express Tribune. According to The Express Tribune, the decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP) at the Quetta Press Club, chaired by ANP provincial president Asghar Khan Achakzai. Participating parties agreed to turn their joint political and democratic struggle into a coordinated movement against what they described as growing public grievances. The leaders also announced a provincial-level meeting on November 26 to determine the next phase of their campaign. An all-parties conference will subsequently be convened in the first week of December to present Balochistan’s pressing concerns before the national leadership. Representatives of the National Party, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, Pashtunkhwa National Awami Party and other political groups attended the gathering. In a joint declaration, the participating parties described the situation in Balochistan as alarming and unacceptable, highlighting persistent insecurity, terrorism, extremism, armed group activities, targeted killings and kidnappings for ransom. They also raised concerns over the unresolved issue of missing persons, unemployment, economic deterioration and difficulties faced by transporters and passengers travelling on national highways. The declaration further blamed the closure of trade and transit routes with Afghanistan and Iran for severely disrupting economic activity across the province. Political leaders also highlighted the impact of soaring inflation, prolonged electricity and gas outages, petroleum levies and restrictions on essential agricultural supplies, including urea fertiliser, as cited by The Express Tribune. They maintained that these measures have adversely affected agriculture, trade, industries and employment. The parties launched a strong attack on the provincial and federal governments, accusing them of failing to protect citizens, maintain law and order, safeguard natural resources and restore economic stability, as reported by The Express Tribune. (ANI)
